scope: Galí, Monetary Policy, Inflation, and the Business Cycle (2nd ed.), Chapter 3: The Basic New Keynesian Model, with Appendices 3.1-3.4 and Exercises 3.1-3.9. Rational expectations as an abstract expectation system with perfect-foresight and finite-event-tree instances; determinacy of two-variable systems via the Schur-Cohn condition; CES demand; the exact Calvo price index and price dispersion; the household's optimality conditions; the reset-price problem over an infinite horizon; marginal cost, the New Keynesian Phillips curve and the dynamic IS equation linked to the nonlinear model as exact derivatives; the Taylor-rule equilibrium with the Bullard-Mitra condition and its unique bounded solution; shock responses; the money-supply rule; calibration; and the exercises.
source: Jordi Galí, Monetary Policy, Inflation, and the Business Cycle: An Introduction to the New Keynesian Framework and Its Applications, 2nd ed., Princeton University Press, 2015, Chapter 3, pp. 52-97.
